value: Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act (VCDPA), Va. Code 59.1-575 et seq. (2021 Acts ch. 35 and 36; HB 2307/SB 1392)
Virginia Attorney General
Residents of Virginia acting in an individual or household context (not commercial or employment context)

Controllers/processors doing business in Virginia or targeting Virginia residents that control or process data of at least 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 consumers plus over 50% of gross revenue from sale of personal data

Consent for sensitive data (59.1-578); rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out of targeted ads/sale/profiling (59.1-577); data protection assessments and reasonable security (59.1-578). No breach-notification duty in the Act
Personal data; sensitive data; pseudonymous data; de-identified data; children's data (under 13, COPPA-aligned)
No fixed period; collection limited to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for the disclosed purpose (59.1-578(A)(1))
Office of the Attorney General of Virginia
Civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation after 30-day cure period; injunctive relief; no private right of action (59.1-584)
Government bodies, financial institutions under GLBA, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofits, higher-education institutions, employment and B2B data (59.1-576)

Colorado Privacy Act (CPA), SB 21-190, C.R.S. 6-1-1301 et seq.
Colorado Attorney General and district attorneys
Residents of Colorado (consumers acting in individual or household context)

Controllers conducting business in Colorado or targeting Colorado residents that process data of 100,000+ consumers per year, or any amount if they derive revenue or discounts from sale of personal data and process 25,000+ consumers
